# L48 — Generalized non-autonomous metric optimization for area coverage problems with mobile autonomous agents

Suruz Miah, Arian Y. Panah, Mostafa Mohammad Hossein Fallah, Davide Spinello; Automatica 80 (2017), 295–299; DOI 10.1016/j.automatica.2017.02.044, as printed. Full extracted PDF pp. 1–5 read; proof independently verifying boundedness/singularities remains pending.

**Task and assumptions:** known smooth positive time-varying density over bounded convex domain, generated by moving targets. First-order point agents know target dynamics and other agents' states (pp. 2–3; conclusion p. 5). Generalized monotone sensing functions and Voronoi cost; no local boundary unknown-map certificate.

**Mechanism/theory:** (7) cancels partial time derivative of coverage using gradient direction divided by squared gradient; Lemma 1 yields monotonic coverage, Proposition 1 invokes Barbalat for generalized-centroid tracking. The denominator can vanish at a stationary gradient while density changes; bounded input and mass/gradient bounds must be examined before adopting its argument. This is a review obligation, not an established disproof.

**Evidence:** eight agents/six moving target simulations, compared with two time-varying coverage laws (p. 4, Figs. 1–2); no physical experiment or repeated success statistics. Authors explicitly leave distributed estimation/communication topology to later work.

**DBACT use:** time-varying density coverage and target-linked density are prior art. Frozen-density dissipation cannot be extended to arbitrary changing local maps without drift/error terms and valid control bounds. Cite as background with its information assumptions, not as proof of DBACT convergence.
